summary: Garrett County, MD tower on Meadow Mountain built 1915 as Maryland's first forestry lookout; FFLA lists it gone and no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookout Association's Maryland list marks it gone; no source read says when it came down or what remains

staffing.status: observer filed daily report cards (state reports for 1918-19); later staffing not in the sources read

events.note: 60-foot tower erected near Bittinger on Meadow Mountain; the DNR report calls it the state's first forestry lookout tower
State forestry reports for 1918 and 1919 say the tower gave efficient service, judged by the observer's daily report cards
Four-mile telephone line built to link the forest guard station at Bond on Savage River with the tower

evidence.supports: 60-foot tower erected in 1915 near Bittinger on Meadow Mountain, Garrett County
evidence.quote: Maryland's first tower detection was provided by a 60-foot tower erected in 1915, near Bittinger, on Meadow Mountain, in Garrett County.

evidence.supports: DNR report: Maryland's first forestry lookout tower was built atop Meadow Mountain in 1915
evidence.quote: Maryland’s first forestry lookout tower was constructed atop Meadow Mountain in 1915.

evidence.quote: It was originally envisioned that 30 to 35 towers would be erected at various high points around the State.

evidence.supports: towers were meant to increase the effectiveness of forest wardens
evidence.quote: that would increase the effectiveness of the forest warden’s efforts.

evidence.supports: 1918-19 state reports: tower gives efficient service, shown by observer's daily report cards
evidence.quote: The lookout tower on Meadow Mountain continues to give efficient service, as evidenced by the observer's daily report cards.

evidence.quote: telephone connection be provided between the guard's station and the Bittinger Forest Fire Tower

the 2007 DNR report covers only towers and tower properties DNR managed as of December 2006

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document

notes_for_editor: Brief staffing 'unknown' replaced with the 1918-19 observer evidence. The 1915 Meadow Mountain tower is tied to the Bittinger record by the Forest Lookouts page and the DNR report's account of the state's first tower; no source read names both together, so the identity is strong but not stated outright. Two web searches and about three page reads; no source gives a removal date or describes the site now. The DNR report also lists a separate Thayerville Tower in Garrett County (standing, Deep Creek Lake State Park, installed 1921). A search snippet had placed Thayerville on Meadow Mountain, but the DNR entry gives no Meadow Mountain location, so this tower is not treated as the Meadow Mountain site; re-check before any visitor link is written.
